title: Bridge check record — v1.0
description: The result of compiling a promoted bridge's bridge_logic to a harness and dispatching that harness to the bridge's owning verifier. plan.md §8.3/§12's G9 row, chainlink #47. One per bridge at ci/results/bridge_checks/<bridge_id>.json, machine-emitted by `pipeline.py check-bridges` -- never hand-authored and never human-reviewed, for the same reason an achieved assurance record carries no review block: a human freely authoring what a verifier 'found' would be indistinguishable from fabricating a result. What makes this a BRIDGE check rather than a harness check is `harness.sha256`: the harness is derived from the promoted bridge_logic by scripts/bridge_harness.py, so the hash can be recomputed from the promoted artifact and compared. plan.md §8.3's temporary alternative pinned a hand-written harness and could only report `harness-tested`; a derived hash pins THIS BRIDGE's harness, which is the machine relation that was missing.

bridge_id.description: Must equal the filename stem exactly (G1b, scripts/gate_g9.py), the same discipline every other artifact in this codebase follows.

verifier.description: The system this harness was compiled FOR and dispatched TO. Checked against the owning verifier of the cluster that requires this bridge (verifier_policy in the project descriptor, resolved through the closure profile that names the work package requiring it) -- a result from a system that does not own the cluster is a cross-verifier composition (CG1), not a check.

sha256.description: Of the generated harness source. Recomputed from the promoted bridge on every gate run; a mismatch means the checked harness is not the one this bridge compiles to, and the result says nothing about this bridge.

dispatch.description: How the verifier was actually invoked. Recorded because 'a verifier checked it' is only meaningful if what ran is visible; a record whose command nobody can read is a claim, not evidence.

record.description: The achieved assurance record for this bridge (docs/achieved-assurance-schema.json), built from the verifier's own verdict. Validated against that schema by scripts/gate_g9.py rather than re-stated here -- one copy of that shape, as with docs/assurance-report-schema.json's own entries.
